correctness.rationale: Derived all three independent-set output probabilities for every \(D_{a,b}\) from independent uniform arrival priorities, including the exact two-variable integral. For fixed n, stars and double-stars exhaust the domain. If a>=2, both center-containing masses are below 1/3, and reciprocal convexity identifies a=2 as the unique best such case; a=1 is optimized separately. Their bias difference equals (\(n^2-8n+9\))/(3n(n-3)(n-2)), negative at n=6 and positive for every n>=7. Direct small-order comparisons give n=3,4,5 and star domination. Fraction-only verifier checks 11 complete permutation enumerations, 20,100 double-star parameter profiles, and all fixed-order minimizers up to n=200; these are corroborating checks and the proof covers every n>=3.

originality.rationale: The main 2026 tree paper gives qualitative nonuniformity and a tuned diameter-four construction, plus the a=1 double-star probability subfamily through its one-arm mixed-spider formula. It does not determine the minimum greedy total-variation bias over every n-vertex tree of diameter at most three, compare arbitrary double stars with two branching centers, or classify all fixed-order minimizers. The new optimization produces the exact all-order bound and unique minimizers, with an exceptional balanced double star at n=6. Related local-limit greedy work concerns expected occupied density rather than this distributional optimum; published cograph/threshold/chain-graph laws do not subsume P4-containing double stars. Targeted scientific searches identified no covering theorem; negative search evidence is not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased prior optimization for greedy maximal-independent-set total variation on double stars might exist.
An exact fixed-order numerical optimum for low n could already be implicit in existing small-tree datasets; the novel scope is the proved all-n classification, not such finite values.
The full text of arxiv:2608.07239 was not accessible in this check; its abstract and the close parent paper discussion were inspected, leaving bounded comparison risk.

value.rationale: The qualitative impossibility of exact greedy output uniformity on nontrivial trees coexists with arbitrarily small bias on diameter-four spiders. Quantifying the precise boundary at diameter three is a natural structural gap. The result determines an exact positive gap and a unique minimizer at every order n>=3, including a balanced-versus-unbalanced phase transition at n=6, rather than an arbitrary small example or mere restatement of a published spider formula. It gives a complete two-branch tree-class optimization; no general all-tree extremizer or new diameter-four family is claimed.
